vision.what: Sets a clear direction for the change and helps people understand what you are trying to achieve.
vision.good: A clear, shared vision that is owned by leaders and understood by those affected.

case_for_change.what: Explains why the change is needed, why it matters and the outcomes it should achieve.
case_for_change.good: A compelling case that creates shared understanding of the need, urgency and expected outcomes.

sponsorship.what: Provides the leadership, accountability and oversight needed to drive the change.
sponsorship.good: Visible, active sponsors with clear accountability, effective governance and timely decision-making.

change_network.what: Connects the change with the people and services affected and provides local insight and support.
change_network.good: An active, representative network that engages people, gathers feedback and supports local adoption.

benefits.what: Defines the improvements expected from the change, who owns them and how they will be measured.
benefits.good: Clear benefits with owners, measures and baselines, linked to the changes needed to achieve them.

change_impact.what: Identifies how the change will affect people, roles, processes, workload and services.
change_impact.good: Impacts are understood early, with actions in place to manage risks and opportunities.

risk_management.what: Identifies and manages the risks and barriers that could affect adoption, benefits or long-term sustainment.
risk_management.good: Adoption risks and barriers are actively identified, owned, monitored and addressed from the start.

cm_readiness.what: Establishes the current change position and the approach needed to support successful adoption.
cm_readiness.good: Baseline findings inform a clear, proportionate change plan aligned with delivery.

stakeholder.what: Ensures people affected by the change are informed, involved and able to provide feedback.
stakeholder.good: Inclusive, timely and two-way engagement tailored to different stakeholder needs.

resistance.what: Identifies and addresses concerns and barriers that could make adoption more difficult.
resistance.good: Concerns and barriers are actively understood, monitored and addressed through targeted action.

skills_learning.what: Builds the knowledge, skills and behaviours people need to work effectively in the new way.
skills_learning.good: Learning is tailored to need and leaves people prepared, capable and supported.

capability.what: Assesses whether people feel able and supported to put the change into practice.
capability.good: People have the confidence, capability and support to apply new ways of working consistently.

change_adoption.what: Assesses whether new ways of working and behaviours are actually being used in practice.
change_adoption.good: Adoption is measured, gaps are addressed and new ways of working are used consistently.

process_change.what: Focuses on whether changed processes are understood, applied and embedded in everyday work.
process_change.good: The new process is consistently followed and supported by the required skills and behaviours.

reinforcement.what: Provides ongoing support, feedback and oversight to help the change stick.
reinforcement.good: New behaviours and processes are recognised, monitored, reinforced and continually improved.

org_maturity.what: Considers the organisation’s wider capability and capacity to lead, learn from and sustain change.
org_maturity.good: Leaders and teams use consistent, repeatable approaches to lead, learn from and embed change.

transfer_bau.what: Moves ownership of the change from the project into routine operational management.
transfer_bau.good: Clear operational ownership is established and the change is embedded into everyday governance and delivery.

benefit_realisation.what: Tracks and evidences the benefits delivered after go-live and keeps them in place.
benefit_realisation.good: Benefits are tracked against baselines, reviewed in governance, evidenced and sustained.
